docs.purpose: A board showing the current verdict of every automated consistency check the project already runs — schema drift, contract drift, the system map, the mobile matrix, golden-file freshness. Those checks exist and pass or fail in CI today, but nothing displays the result where an operator would see it. A check nobody reads is a check nobody acts on, and this page is the reader.
docs.data_story: Nothing is built yet, so nothing is measured here. As specified it reads descriptor files and checker verdicts rather than database tables.
docs.under_126: **NEW.** It does not exist; it is generated from descriptors from its first commit, through the DASHBOARD renderer (tiles that each declare their own contract and degrade independently). It is **100% generated** — which is the point: if the descriptor set is incomplete or an archetype profile is wrong, this page is visibly empty or visibly wrong on commit 1, and cannot be faked by hand.

checks.why: A checker whose output shape changed must render as schema_drift on its own tile — a drift dashboard that silently drops a drifted checker is self-refuting.
A tile that cannot compute renders "unavailable" in place, never a blank cell and never taking the grid with it (Spec 128 rule 12: an unhandled state is a FAIL, not a blank screen).
Zero tiles means the checker registry is unseeded, which must not read as "no drift".
One of the tiles IS this check — census Q15, surface.guards.session vs contract.guards.auth_class — and Spec 126 §6.2 rule 3 puts it at FAIL.
Rule 14's both-directions catalog assertion is a tile: a column live but undeclared fails exactly as a column declared but absent does.
Rule 15's golden-pair equality is a tile too — the promise "100% data parity" is a diff, and this is where the diff is read.
Permanently non-zero while artifacts are regenerated on a commit cadence rather than a clock; the retighten condition is a per-artifact declared bound.
A verdict conveyed only by tile colour is unreadable to a screen reader and to anyone with a colour-vision deficiency.

limitations.what: The DASHBOARD required-field profile in Spec 126 §3.1 mandates tiles[] each with its own contract_ref and degrade_independently, plus refresh.poll_ms and per-tile states[], and surface.schema.json has no property for any of them (the top level and every category are additionalProperties:false).
limitations.measured: Every allOf block in scripts/surfaces/_schema/surface.schema.json is `"then": true` — the archetype profiles are declared in prose in Spec 126 §3.1 and enforced by nothing, so these fields can neither be declared here nor caught missing.

limitations.what: plausibility is "none" on a surface whose whole job is verdicts.
limitations.measured: plausibility takes declarative SQL only, and a checker verdict has no SQL expression — the same reason R-34 keeps ad/layout policy in checks[] rather than plausibility[]. The verdicts are therefore checks[] entries, which is where they belong.
